newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS RISE FURTHER, CROWN SOFTENS.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS RISE FURTHER, CROWN SOFTENS.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose further at midday on Wednesday, pushed up by weaker U.S. and German markets, while the crown softened against a generally stronger mark.
"We traded on higher U.S. interest rates overnight and weaker European markets, primarily Germany, early in the session," one dealer said.
He expected the market to calm down ahead of U.S. July retail sales and producer prices, due at 1230 GMT.
The market was hurt by the Bundesbank's monthly report and the Bavarian premier Stoiber's talk of delaying EMU to 2001.

The Bundesbank warned in its August report that the pace of consumer price increases had picked up in the last few months and that it would be aiming its policy to ensure inflation remained under control.
The 10-year bond yield rose six basis points to 6.59 percent while the six-month T-bill rate climbed two basis points to 4.33 percent.
The crown softened to 4.3260 against the generally stronger mark from 4.2990 late on Tuesday.
